theorem_statement: Theorem (filtered balanced CE rank ideals and fibre dimensions at (g,n)=(6,6)). Let k be a characteristic-zero field, B a locally Noetherian k-scheme, π:C→B a smooth proper family with geometrically connected genus-six fibres, and Γ the union of six pairwise-disjoint sections. Assume the balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl data induce the canonical filtration 0→W_4→W→W_5→0, where W_4 and W_5 are invertible of fibre degrees 20 and 16. Let φ:π_*W→π_*(W|_Γ) and φ_5:π_*W_5→π_*(W_5|_Γ), put N=ω_{C/B}⊗W_5^∨(Γ), and let a_N:B→Pic^0_{C/B} classify N with e the identity section. Then the graded evaluation maps have ranks 15→6 and 11→6, φ has ranks 26→12, and, without any global splitting of W, Fit_0(coker φ)=I_12(φ)=I_6(φ_5)=a_N^*I_e scheme-theoretically and compatibly with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change. Moreover I_11(φ)=O_B and I_5(φ_5)=O_B, so every geometric fibre has rank 12 or 11 for φ and rank 6 or 5 for φ_5, with no deeper rank drop. Under the additional standard CE-resolution and equation-bundle finite-local-freeness/base-change hypotheses of ATT-0065, the ambient CE evaluation has the same cokernel and determinantal failure scheme. For a geometric fibre C_b, put L_b=W_{5,b}⊗ω_{C_b}^{-1} and M_b=ω_{C_b}^{⊗2}⊗W_{5,b}^∨. As an effective divisor D ranges through Sym^6(C_b), the geometric rank-drop set is exactly |L_b|; φ_D has rank 11 precisely when O_{C_b}(D)≅L_b and rank 12 otherwise. One has deg M_b=4 and h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b), hence 1≤h^0(L_b)≤4 and dim|L_b|=h^0(L_b)−1∈{0,1,2,3}; its codimension in Sym^6(C_b) is 7−h^0(L_b)∈{3,4,5,6}. The equality h^0(L_b)=4 holds exactly when C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b is the square of its hyperelliptic g^1_2. The ordered distinct-support fibre is a finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in |L_b|; it is either empty or has dimension h^0(L_b)−1.
